suites.description:
The Change Log is public facing (account menu -> Change Log) and the account
menu also prints "App last updated" from SJ_APP_UPDATED_FALLBACK. A push hook
already refuses a push whose newest entry is not dated today; that is a rule
about the push. These are rules about the DATA, and they hold at any moment:
the two dates agree, the list runs newest first, nothing is dated in the
future, and no entry is empty or written for engineers.

tests.name: App last updated is the date of the newest entry, not a date of its own
every entry has at least one item, and no item is a commit subject

(title, artist, album, length) and gets back one track id, so everything
that decides which song a file IS lives in resolveCandidate. These cover the
shapes real folders arrive in: proper tags, a raw YouTube upload title on
our side, no artist at all, and two bands with the same song name.

suites.description:
The room's queue IS the host's ytQueue seen from outside. The host pushes its
whole queue every five seconds and reconcileHostQueue works out the
difference. The awkward part is telling a song the host DELETED apart from a
song a guest added a second ago, and getting that backwards means a host who
reloads their tab wipes the whole room's requests. These cover both sides of
that line.

tests.name: a drag to the very front of the waiting list reports no song to sit behind
a first push writes the queue in, one row per song, with room to drag between
a host that just reloaded adopts everything and sweeps nothing
a played or removed row is never swept, only pending and playing ones
a row a guest dragged since the last push is left alone, not snapped home
a row created since the host last checked in is a guest add, so it is adopted
a row the host used to have and no longer sends is a deletion to honour
a song already taken out of the room wins over a host still holding it
a song the host played before the room existed is never written in
a song with no catalogue track is not mirrorable and stays private to the host
a track change writes the two rows that moved and nothing else
in the steady state a host pushing the same queue writes nothing at all
status is derived from position alone, so there is no advance call to get out of step

a station left advertising itself with nothing playing eventually closes
a stuck client cannot write a nonsense position into the room
a typed name cannot break the TV layout, and is not otherwise filtered
an empty playback blob normalizes to the documented empty state
anybody who has stopped polling is dropped, not greyed out
extrapolation never runs off the end of the song, and a pause does not move
guests are never given a name, they are given a number
how long somebody has been here is this stretch, not the night they first scanned
opening the room hours before the music starts is not an expired broadcast
playback strings are trimmed, capped and blanked rather than stored raw

suites.covers: ytQueueSignature, ytMoveToIndex, ytMoveAfterCurrent, ytPlayNextIndex in public/index.html
suites.description:
A 2,600 song queue made every player update cost half a second of blocked
main thread, and moving a row by arithmetic pointed the player at somebody
else's song. Both fixes are load-bearing and neither is visible from the
outside: a signature that is missing a field silently costs a listener their
name on a row, and an index re-found by arithmetic silently plays the wrong
track. These pin both down.

suites.description:
Adding a jukebox view means three edits in three files, matched by shot_id
and nothing else. When they disagree the app does not error: the export modal
offers a picture the nightly job never built, so it silently falls through to
drawing in a hidden iframe - slow on a desktop, broken on a phone. That is
exactly what happened to Timeline / Tracks Open, By Views / Tracks Open and
Albums List on 2026-08-23. This is the guard against the next one.

gaps.detail: Every rule in src/lib/jukebox.ts is covered, but nothing exercises /api/jukebox/*. The guest seat cookie, the owner access token check and the service-role writes are all unproven by the suite.

buildAlbumFromSongs, the three-pass YouTube search and albumIdentityScore live in a Supabase edge function, not in this repo's build. The workspace copy goes stale, so a test against it would prove something about a file nobody deploys.

spi* is only reachable with a sealed session cookie and a live Spotify account. Nothing covers the /items versus /tracks trap, the notOwned versus reconnect split, or the 429 retry that stops a throttled pass being reported as songs not found.

gaps.gap: Row level security and the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs
gaps.detail: can_edit_track_videos, can_manage_artist, landing_stats visibility filtering and the jukebox_* service-role-only grants are enforced in Postgres. A policy written without a grant verifies nothing, and only a live database can say so.
The three shot lists are checked against each other, but nothing drives Playwright. A shot that silently goes blank because a page global was renamed still only turns up in the morning's images.

gaps.gap: Anything that needs a real YouTube player
gaps.detail: Queue order, shuffle weighting and the Play next override are covered as pure logic. The IFrame API, background play, CarPlay handoff and crossfade timing are not, and cannot be without a browser.
Render functions are asserted by reading their source rather than by mounting them. That catches a deleted guard or a renamed global; it does not catch markup that renders wrong.
set_my_settings carries a new public name onto every credit already written across nine tables. Nothing here proves it reaches all nine.
